newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Greenalls held back by northern pubs.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Greenalls held back by northern pubs.

text.p: British pubs-to-hotel company Greenalls Group Plc posted a 12 percent increase in its half year profits on Monday to 63.9 million pounds ($104.7 million) excluding exceptional items, held back by difficult trading conditions at some of its drinks-led pubs in the North West of England.

Exceptional charges amounted to 6.2 million, including pub reorganisation costs of 7.3 million which the group announced in March. Brokers forecasts for pretax profits ranged from 61.1 million to 66.0 million.
"(Perhaps) it's the strength of the pound putting pressure on the manufactoring sector, which means there may be less disposable income available," chief executive Lord Daresbury told Reuters.
"Moving 245 pubs to tenanted was aimed at sorting this out. These are pubs in secondary locations. I think that move is a radical move and it has addressed the problem," he added.
Greenalls will spend 25 million pounds more on expanding its pub restaurant and managed pubs, Village Leisure and De Vere's golf hotels next year, he said.
The group's total capital expenditure programme will rise to 200 million pounds next year from 175 million.
"This expenditure is currently 70 percent offensive and 30 percent defensive, in other words spent on maintenance, but next year we will spend 150 million offensively as against 125," he added.
Daresbury said the company has made further progress since its half year results, "its very much the same as before, satisfactory and we are hoping that will continue."

The group's pubs and restaurants division reported a 12.7 percent increase in trading profit to 45.1 million stg. Profits from its de Vere hotels rose 19.4 percent to 12.7 million, with the hotels and leisure division as whole posting a 28 percent increase in profits to 16.66 million.
De Vere hotels achieved room rates 15.9 percent higher at 62 pounds and the company plans to develop its golf hotels where returns are higher.
"Our hotel figures compare very well with Stakis and Vaux and Marriott RevPar Whitbread announced was up only 16 percent," said Daresbury.
Greenalls franchised pubs and wholesaling business reported a 12.7 percent improvement in trading profit to 24.3 million.
The company's shares were off 1/2p at 493-1/2 in early trade, against the background of a softer London stockmarket.

"The results were in line, probably a touch better than our estimates, but there is a question mark over cash generation and returns on their capital expenditure programme," said Panmure Gordon analyst James Wheatcroft. Net cash inflow fell to 67.4 million in the 26 weeks to March 28, 1997 down from 77.652 million previously.
